theorem.statement:
Assume ass:density-positivity, ass:density-smoothness, ass:inner-ellipticity, ass:outer-ellipticity, ass:lift-regularity, ass:fixed-separated-grid, ass:kernel-symmetry, ass:kernel-mass, ass:kernel-order, ass:four-sample-design, ass:cell-ratios, and ass:polynomial-bandwidth.  Fix \(s\geq 8\) and
\[
 \frac{1}{2(s-2)}\leq a_h<\frac16.
\]
After \(a_h\) is fixed, choose \(\vartheta\in(0,1)\) so that \(a_h(6+4\vartheta)<1\), and define, for \(k\in\{0,1,2\}\),
\[
 q_{k,n}(\vartheta)
 =\sqrt{\frac{\log n}{n h_n^{,2+2k+2\vartheta}}}
   +h_n^{,s-k-\vartheta}.
\]
Then there is a finite constant \(C_\star\), independent of \(P\) and \(n\), for which the program \(\mathfrak H_{\mathrm{crit}}\) gives the following conclusions uniformly over \(P\in\mathcal F_s\).

First, if \(\Psi^{\mathrm{fr}}_{g,h_n}\) denotes the centered frozen-coefficient, affine-coordinate, frozen-pole part of the exact score \(\Psi_{g,h_n}\), then
\[
 \max_{g\in\mathcal G}
 \left\|\Psi_{g,h_n}-\Psi^{\mathrm{fr}}_{g,h_n}\right\|_{L^2(P_g)}
 \leq C_\star,
\tag{1}
\]
and both the second elliptic response in \(\mathcal D_P\) and the complete scalar--harmonic response \(\mathcal H_P\) have cellwise \(L^2(P_g)\) norms bounded by \(C_\star\).  Consequently,
\[
 \sup_{P\in\mathcal F_s}\max_{g\in\mathcal G}
 \frac{1}{L_n}
 \left\|
  \operatorname{Var}_{P_g}(\Psi_{g,h_n})
  -\operatorname{Var}_{P_g}(\Psi^{\mathrm{fr}}_{g,h_n})
 \right\|_{\mathrm{op}}
 \longrightarrow0.
\tag{2}
\]
More explicitly, choose a coordinate ball \(U_j\) about \(y_j\), and a fixed smooth cutoff \(\chi_j\) supported in \(U_j\) and equal to one on a smaller ball.  At the pole \(y_j\) put
\[
 \Gamma_j(z)=-\frac{1}{2\pi\sqrt{\det B(y_j)}}
 \log\left|B(y_j)^{-1/2}(z-y_j)\right|.
\tag{2a}
\]
Then the computable frozen-pole energy is
\[
 \frac1{L_n}\int_{\mathbb T^2}
 \{K_{h_n}^{\mathrm{per}}*(\chi_j\nabla\Gamma_j)\}(z)
 \{K_{h_n}^{\mathrm{per}}*(\chi_j\nabla\Gamma_j)\}(z)^{\mathsf T}\,dz
 \longrightarrow
 \frac{B(y_j)^{-1}}{4\pi\sqrt{\det B(y_j)}}.
\tag{2b}
\]
Thus the full transformed-KDE variable-coefficient response has the frozen-pole logarithmic covariance, with every generated-target within-cell cross term retained.

Second, for the opposite-fold plug-in scores,
\[
 \sup_{P\in\mathcal F_s}
 \mathbb P_P\!\left{
 \max_{g\in\mathcal G,\ r\in\{1,2\}}
 L_n^{-1/2}
 \left\|\widehat\Psi_{g,h_n}^{(-r)}-\Psi_{g,h_n}\right\|_{L^2(P_g)}
 >\epsilon\right}\longrightarrow0
\tag{3}
\]
for every \(\epsilon>0\).  This includes estimated-coefficient, moving-pole, and selected-lift errors; clipping and the measurable fallback occur with probability tending to zero uniformly.

Third, put \(u_n=(\widetilde f_g-f_g)_{g\in\mathcal G}\) and
\[
 R_{n,j}
 =\widetilde T_{P+u_n}(\widetilde y_j)
  -\widetilde T_P(\widetilde y_j)-\mathcal D_P[u_n]_j.
\]
Then
\[
 \sup_{P\in\mathcal F_s}
 \mathbb P_P\!\left{
 \sqrt{\frac n{L_n}}\max_{1\leq j\leq J}\|R_{n,j}|>\epsilon
 \right}\longrightarrow0,
\tag{4}
\]
and the deterministic order-minus-two bias satisfies
\[
 \sqrt{\frac n{L_n}}h_n^{s-2}\longrightarrow0.
\tag{5}
\]
The bound behind (4) is the mixed two-endpoint estimate
\[
 \max_j|R_{n,j}|
 \leq C_\star\left(\max_g\|u_{n,g}\|_{C^{1,\vartheta}}\right)
          \left(\max_g\|u_{n,g}\|_{C^{0,\vartheta}}\right),
\tag{6}
\]
not a squared \(C^{1,\vartheta}\) bound.  The window above is maximal for these synchronized polynomial conditions: \(q_{2,n}(\vartheta)=o(1)\) and \(q_{0,n}(\vartheta)/h_n=o(1)\) are weaker, whereas
\(\sqrt{n/L_n}\,q_{1,n}(\vartheta)q_{0,n}(\vartheta)\to0\) is binding, and \(a_h=1/6\) is excluded.
theorem.proof_tex:
Fix \(a_h<1/6\).  Since \(a_h>0\), the interval
\[
 0<\vartheta<\min\left\{1,\frac{a_h^{-1}-6}{4}\right\}
\tag{7}
\]
is nonempty; hence a fixed \(\vartheta\) satisfying \(a_h(6+4\vartheta)<1\) exists.  For later reference, the product of the two stochastic parts of \(q_{1,n}(\vartheta)\) and \(q_{0,n}(\vartheta)\), after critical normalization, is
\[
 \sqrt{\frac n{L_n}}
 \sqrt{\frac{\log n}{n h_n^{4+2\vartheta}}}
 \sqrt{\frac{\log n}{n h_n^{2+2\vartheta}}}
 =a_h^{-1/2}(\log n)^{1/2}
   n^{-1/2+a_h(3+2\vartheta)}.
\tag{8}
\]
The exponent on \(n\) in (8) is negative precisely when
\(a_h(6+4\vartheta)<1\).  Lem:mixed-bandwidth-feasibility expands the other three nonnegative products and proves that, under \(s\geq8\) and the lower bound \(a_h\geq1/[2(s-2)]\), they vanish as well.  The same lemma gives
\[
 \sqrt{\frac n{L_n}}h_n^{s-2}\to0,
 \qquad q_{2,n}(\vartheta)  o0,
 \qquad \frac{q_{0,n}(\vartheta)}{h_n}  o0,
 \qquad
 \sqrt{\frac n{L_n}}q_{1,n}(\vartheta)q_{0,n}(\vartheta)  o0.
\tag{9}
\]
At \(a_h=1/6\), the right side of (8) equals
\(a_h^{-1/2}(\log n)^{1/2}n^{\vartheta/3}\) for every admissible \(\vartheta>0\), and even the formal endpoint \(\vartheta=0\) leaves the divergent factor \((\log n)^{1/2}\).  Thus the endpoint cannot be included.  Lem:mixed-bandwidth-feasibility also proves that the conditions involving \(q_{2,n}\) and \(q_{0,n}/h_n\) impose strictly weaker upper restrictions, establishing the asserted maximality.

We next invoke the analytic conclusion of lem:uniform-critical-estimates, whose hypotheses are exactly the maintained positivity, smoothness, ellipticity, lift-margin, separated-grid, kernel, sampling, and bandwidth conditions listed in the theorem.  That lemma constructs the periodic Green parametrix after pulling every kernel tangent to the original cell coordinate.  In its notation, the exact centered score admits
\[
 \Psi_{g,h_n}=\Psi^{\mathrm{fr}}_{g,h_n}+E_{g,n},
 \qquad
 \sup_{P\in\mathcal F_s}\max_{g\in\mathcal G}
 \|E_{g,n}\|_{L^2(P_g)}\leq C,
\tag{10}
\]
and
\[
 \sup_{P\in\mathcal F_s}\max_g
 \|\Psi^{\mathrm{fr}}_{g,h_n}\|_{L^2(P_g)}
 \leq C\sqrt{L_n}.
\tag{11}
\]
Equation (10) includes the order-minus-two generated-target response and, by thm:nested-derivative, the complete inner and outer harmonic correction rather than setting either translation derivative to zero.  This proves (1) and the two stated componentwise \(L^2\) bounds.

For centered square-integrable random vectors \(X\) and \(E\), Cauchy--Schwarz gives
\[
 \|\operatorname{Var}(X+E)-\operatorname{Var}(X)\|_{\mathrm{op}}
 \leq 2\|X\|_{L^2}\|E\|_{L^2}+\|E\|_{L^2}^2.
\tag{12}
\]
Apply (12) with \(X=\Psi^{\mathrm{fr}}_{g,h_n}\) and \(E=E_{g,n}\).  Equations (10)--(11) imply
\[
 \sup_{P\in\mathcal F_s}\max_g
 \frac{1}{L_n}
 \|\operatorname{Var}_{P_g}(\Psi_{g,h_n})
   -\operatorname{Var}_{P_g}(\Psi^{\mathrm{fr}}_{g,h_n})\|_{\mathrm{op}}
 \leq \frac{C}{\sqrt{L_n}}+\frac{C}{L_n}\to0,
\tag{13}
\]
because \(L_n=a_h\log n\to\infty\).  The frozen term in lem:uniform-critical-estimates is obtained by freezing only inside the energy parametrix.  To compute its covariance, write \(B_j=B(y_j)\).  Away from the pole, (2a) gives
\[
 \nabla\Gamma_j(z)
 =-\frac{1}{2\pi\sqrt{\det B_j}}
 \frac{B_j^{-1}(z-y_j)}{(z-y_j)^{\mathsf T}B_j^{-1}(z-y_j)}.
\tag{13a}
\]
With \(z-y_j=B_j^{1/2}r\omega\), \(\omega\in\mathbb S^1\), one has
\(dz=\sqrt{\det B_j}\,r\,dr\,d\omega\) and
\(\int_{\mathbb S^1}\omega\omega^{\mathsf T}d\omega=\pi I_2\).  Hence, for fixed small \(r_0\),
\[
 \int_{h_n<|B_j^{-1/2}(z-y_j)|<r_0}
 \nabla\Gamma_j(z)\nabla\Gamma_j(z)^{\mathsf T}\,dz
 =\frac{B_j^{-1}}{4\pi\sqrt{\det B_j}}L_n+O(1).
\tag{13b}
\]
Lem:uniform-critical-estimates proves uniformly that periodic mollification and the replacement of the elliptical annulus by a coordinate neighborhood change (13b) by \(o(L_n)\).  This proves (2b).  Consequently (13) proves (2), including the transformed-kernel and variable-coefficient replacement.  Since the four samples are independent by ass:four-sample-design, cross-cell covariances vanish; since each cell score is formed before its variance is taken, no within-cell generated-target cross product is discarded.

The opposite-fold part of lem:uniform-critical-estimates states, for every \(\epsilon>0\), exactly
\[
 \sup_{P\in\mathcal F_s}\mathbb P_P\!\left{
 \max_{g,r}L_n^{-1/2}
 \|\widehat\Psi_{g,h_n}^{(-r)}-\Psi_{g,h_n}\|_{L^2(P_g)}
 >\epsilon\right}\to0.
\tag{14}
\]
Its proof uses \(q_{2,n}=o(1)\) for coefficient stability and
\(q_{0,n}/h_n=o(1)\) for the moving-pole Taylor bound.  It also shows that density clipping is inactive, normalization equals one, and ass:lift-regularity keeps both estimated maps on the selected population branch outside an event of uniformly vanishing probability.  Therefore (14) is precisely (3), including every error named there.

Finally, on the common good event supplied by lem:uniform-critical-estimates, the translation-aware two-endpoint expansion from thm:nested-derivative yields
\[
 \max_{1\leq j\leq J}|R_{n,j}|
 \leq C U_{1,n}(\vartheta)U_{0,n}(\vartheta),
 \qquad
 U_{k,n}(\vartheta)=\max_{g\in\mathcal G}
 \|u_{n,g}\|_{C^{k,\vartheta}}.
\tag{15}
\]
The moment and tail estimates in lem:uniform-critical-estimates give
\[
 U_{k,n}(\vartheta)=O_{\mathbb P}(q_{k,n}(\vartheta))
 \quad(k=0,1,2)
\tag{16}
\]
uniformly over \(\mathcal F_s\), and the complement of the good event has uniformly vanishing probability.  Combining (9), (15), and (16) gives, for every \(\epsilon>0\),
\[
 \sup_{P\in\mathcal F_s}\mathbb P_P\!\left{
 \sqrt{\frac n{L_n}}\max_j|R_{n,j}|>\epsilon\right}\to0,
\tag{17}
\]
which is (4).  The first limit in (9) is (5).  Equations (10), (13), (14), and (17) establish every item asked by the open-ended question, so the answer is affirmative on the maximal open polynomial bandwidth window.

proposed_core_edits.proposed: \(\widehat\tau=(-\widehat a_T-\nabla\widehat\phi_T(\widetilde y_j))_{j=1}^J,\qquad \sqrt{n/L_n}\{\widehat\tau-\tau(P)\}\Rightarrow N(0,V(P))\), uniformly over the maintained class.
proposed_core_edits.reason: The uniform critical-control question is resolved, so the headline functional must state the proved Gaussian limit rather than call it a candidate conditional on an open obligation.

proposed.comparator_claim: Proposition 29 proves a \(\sqrt{n/\log(1/h_n)}\) pointwise Gaussian limit with covariance \(I_2/(4\pi)\) when source and target are uniform on \(\mathbb T^2\).  The present result recovers that constant in the known-cell reduction and extends the dimension-two phenomenon only on the stronger smooth, positive, uniformly elliptic, selected-no-cut, fixed-grid, independent-four-sample torus class.

Theorem 3.2 differentiates a Brenier map along one smooth target-density curve through a linearized Monge--Ampere problem; the present derivative treats two varying endpoints, nonzero selected torus translations, four inputs, and a generated target.

Theorem 2 and Corollary 1 identify the multivariate changes-in-changes counterfactual on proper convex Euclidean supports under cyclic comonotonicity.  The intrinsic squared-distance flat-torus identification here is a distinct theorem, not an extension of that Euclidean support result.

Section 3, Theorems 3.1 and 3.3 identify a gradient-Green influence and its pole singularity, but do not prove the shrinking-bandwidth four-sample nested empirical central limit theorem established here.
Theorems 2.4 and 2.10 give a weak functional limit and bootstrap for empirical Brenier potentials and fixed weighted contrasts, not pointwise gradients.

Theorems 2 and 6 give near-matching global \(L^2\) minimax rates for one smooth transport map through wavelet semi-dual estimation and a Fano lower bound; the present result instead gives a nested fixed-grid Hellinger-local logarithmic rate.
Theorem 18 gives a \(\log n/n\) global squared-risk upper rate for a two-dimensional smooth-density plug-in map without the fixed-grid nested Hellinger-local lower bound proved here.

Theorem 3 and Corollary 4 validate a smoothed bootstrap uniform band for a one-dimensional quantile-represented transport map; the present confidence sets are bivariate but only on a fixed separated grid.

Theorems 2--4 and Corollary 2 derive efficient root-\(n\) inference for scalar effects and distributional estimands under a distributional bridge in paired panel data; neither their estimand nor their dependent sampling design is claimed here.

proposed_core_edits.reason: The analytic gate is now proved, so the comparator audit must distinguish the two results that are directly tightened from the sources that remain scope-setting only.

prose_updates.tldr: Under the intrinsic flat-torus changes-in-changes assumptions, the observed nested Brenier functional is proved to equal the selected-lift no-treatment displacement.  For four independent smooth positive samples and the order-\(s\) positive-normalized periodized KDE, the uniform variable-coefficient Green analysis closes on the maximal polynomial window \(1/[2(s-2)]\leq a_h<1/6\).  It yields the full four-cell covariance, the \(\sqrt{n/L_n}\) fixed-grid Gaussian limit, consistent cross-fitted adjoint covariance, simultaneous multiplier ellipses, and matching \(L_n/n\) squared-risk upper and Hellinger-local lower rates.

project_justification.gap: Published changes-in-changes identification on proper convex Euclidean supports does not establish the intrinsic squared-distance torus result, and published transport limit theory does not supply a four-input, generated-target, pointwise-gradient critical law with moving estimated poles and nonzero harmonic translations.
project_justification.niche: In dimension two the Green gradient has logarithmic energy.  Pulling both inner and generated-target equations into treated-post coordinates reduces the singular nested derivative to one outer Green response to four independent cell noises, while the second elliptic response and the selected-translation scores remain bounded in \(L^2\).
project_justification.fill: The note proves the intrinsic identification, the augmented scalar--harmonic derivative, the uniform transformed-kernel parametrix and mixed \(C^{1,\vartheta}\)-by-\(C^{0,\vartheta}\) remainder, the full generated-target covariance, the joint critical Gaussian law, feasible adjoint inference, and matching rate bounds.  The synchronized bandwidth condition is maximal for this proof and excludes \(a_h=1/6\).

sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: Each of the four independent cell densities is estimated by the declared order-\(s\) signed periodized KDE, clipped at \(c/2\) and renormalized; on the uniform good event clipping is inactive and the normalizer equals one.  A fixed \(a_h\) is chosen in \(1/[2(s-2)],1/6)\), followed by a fixed \(\vartheta>0\) satisfying \(a_h(6+4\vartheta)<1\).  The map and covariance calculations solve the augmented scalar--harmonic systems, use opposite-fold adjoint pilots, retain all generated-target cross products, and add \(n^{-1}I_{2J}\) before block inversion.

prose_updates.related_work: TorousGunsiliusRigollet2024OTCiC proves changes-in-changes identification on proper convex Euclidean supports; the intrinsic squared-geodesic full-support flat-torus identification here is separate and is not presented as an extension of that theorem.  Relative to Proposition 29 of ManoleBalakrishnanNilesWeedWasserman2023CLT, this note generalizes the dimension-two pointwise phenomenon only on the stronger smooth, positive, uniformly elliptic, selected-no-cut, fixed-grid, independent-four-sample torus class, and its known-cell uniform reduction recovers \(I_2/(4\pi)\).  GonzalezSanzSheng2024Linearization supplies a one-density-path linearization; the present weighted-Hodge argument handles two varying endpoints, translations, and a generated target.  The 2026 Green-influence and potential-limit results do not themselves give the nested shrinking-bandwidth pointwise-gradient law proved here.  HutterRigollet2021Minimax and ManoleBalakrishnanNilesWeedWasserman2024Plugin concern global one-map risk, whereas the present converse is fixed-center Hellinger-local and the upper risk is for the nested fixed-grid plug-in.  PonnopratOkanoImaizumi2024UniformBand concerns a one-dimensional uniform band; the present ellipses are bivariate and simultaneous only over a fixed grid.
prose_updates.interpretation: The causal target is the selected-lift no-treatment treated-post displacement, whereas \(P\mapsto\tau(P)\) is an observed-law nested optimal-transport functional.  Lem:torus-cic-identification proves their equality under ass:cic-identification and ass:lift-regularity; outside those structural conditions the functional is not assigned a causal meaning.  At a grid point \(y_j\), the limiting block is \(V_j=w_j\sqrt{\det H(y_j)}H(y_j)/(4\pi f_{T1}(y_j))\), where the two control contributions include their generated-target cross terms before squaring.  Distinct fixed-grid points are asymptotically independent, while harmonic translations affect finite-bandwidth covariance but vanish after logarithmic normalization.  Because the limiting blocks are independent and each standardized block is \(\chi^2_2\), the simultaneous deterministic critical value is \(c_{J,\gamma}=-2\log\{1-(1-\gamma)^{1/J}\}\).
prose_updates.technical_internal_limitation: The proofs require a two-dimensional flat torus, \(C^s\) densities with \(s\geq8\), common positive density bounds, uniformly elliptic population transports, a selected lift uniformly separated from lattice boundaries and the squared-distance cut locus, four independent samples with stable size ratios, and a fixed separated evaluation grid.  The maximal synchronized polynomial window is open at \(1/6\); at the endpoint the stochastic--stochastic mixed remainder does not vanish.  The result does not cover nonperiodic domains, cut-locus crossings, dependent panels, growing grids, unsmoothed empirical optimal transport, or data-driven bandwidth selection outside the proved window.
prose_updates.honest_scope: The note certifies an observed-law functional and its causal interpretation only under the intrinsic torus changes-in-changes representation, then proves fixed-grid Gaussian inference and an \(L_n/n\) rate match on the stronger smooth positive uniformly elliptic selected-no-cut independent-four-sample class.  It does not claim semiparametric efficiency or an exact minimax constant.  A Card--Krueger bivariate employment reanalysis would additionally require a prespecified periodic encoding of the two outcomes, a defensible repeated-cross-section independence approximation, diagnostics for positivity, branch separation and ellipticity, and numerical PDE and adjoint errors negligible relative to \(\sqrt{L_n/n}\).

statement_notes.justification: The theorem resolves the open question affirmatively by collecting the exact covariance replacement, plug-in score stability, and nonlinear remainder consequences of the uniform estimates.
statement_notes.gap: No residual transformed-KDE or moving-pole obligation remains under the maintained maximal bandwidth regime.
statement_notes.consumer: It discharges the analytic gate for the paper's complete inference and risk spine.

proofs.proof_tex:
For the parameterized calculation, fix \(0<\vartheta<1\) and put
\[
 q_{k,n}(\vartheta)
 =A_{k,n}(\vartheta)+D_{k,n}(\vartheta),\qquad
 A_{k,n}(\vartheta)
 =\left\{\frac{\log n}{n h_n^{2+2k+2\vartheta}}\right\}^{1/2},
 \qquad
 D_{k,n}(\vartheta)=h_n^{s-k-\vartheta},
 \quad k=0,1,2.
\tag{1}
\]
All summands in (1) are nonnegative.  Since \(h_n=n^{-a_h}\) and
\(L_n=a_h\log n\), the bias condition is
\[
 \sqrt{\frac n{L_n}}h_n^{s-2}
 =\frac{n^{1/2-a_h(s-2)}}{\sqrt{a_h\log n}}\longrightarrow0
 \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
 a_h\geq\frac1{2(s-2)}.
\tag{2}
\]
Equality is allowed in (2), because then the numerator's power of \(n\) is zero and the logarithmic denominator diverges.

The two requirements used for pilot and pole stability are weaker than the mixed requirement.  Indeed,
\[
 A_{2,n}(\vartheta)
 =\sqrt{\log n}\,n^{-1/2+a_h(3+\vartheta)},
 \qquad
 \frac{A_{0,n}(\vartheta)}{h_n}
 =\sqrt{\log n}\,n^{-1/2+a_h(2+\vartheta)}.
\tag{3}
\]
Thus \(q_{2,n}(\vartheta)=o(1)\) if
\(a_h<1/(6+2\vartheta)\), and
\(q_{0,n}(\vartheta)/h_n=o(1)\) if
\(a_h<1/(4+2\vartheta)\); their deterministic parts vanish because
\(s-2-\vartheta>0\) and \(s-1-\vartheta>0\) for \(s\geq8\) and
\(0<\vartheta<1\).

Expanding the product in the binding condition gives four nonnegative terms.  The stochastic--stochastic term is
\[
 \sqrt{\frac n{L_n}}A_{1,n}(\vartheta)A_{0,n}(\vartheta)
 =a_h^{-1/2}\sqrt{\log n}\,
   n^{-1/2+a_h(3+2\vartheta)}.
\tag{4}
\]
It converges to zero exactly when
\[
 a_h<\frac1{6+4\vartheta}.
\tag{5}
\]
The two stochastic--bias terms are identical after normalization:
\[
 \sqrt{\frac n{L_n}}A_{1,n}(\vartheta)D_{0,n}(\vartheta)
 =\sqrt{\frac n{L_n}}D_{1,n}(\vartheta)A_{0,n}(\vartheta)
 =a_h^{-1/2}h_n^{s-2-2\vartheta}=o(1).
\tag{6}
\]
The last equality follows from \(s\geq8\) and \(\vartheta<1\).  Finally,
\[
 \sqrt{\frac n{L_n}}D_{1,n}(\vartheta)D_{0,n}(\vartheta)
 =\frac{n^{1/2-a_h(2s-1-2\vartheta)}}{\sqrt{a_h\log n}}.
\tag{7}
\]
Under the lower bound in (2), the power in (7) is strictly negative, since
\(2s-1-2\vartheta>s-2\).  Hence (5) is the only upper restriction.  It also implies both upper restrictions following (3), because
\(6+4\vartheta>6+2\vartheta\) and
\(6+4\vartheta>4+2\vartheta\).

Now fix \(a_h\).  If
\[
 \frac1{2(s-2)}\leq a_h<\frac16,
\tag{8}
\]
then \(a_h^{-1}-6>0\), so one may choose once and for all
\[
 0<\vartheta<\min\left\{1,\frac{a_h^{-1}-6}{4}\right\}.
\tag{9}
\]
For this choice, (5) holds, and (2)--(7) prove
\[
 \sqrt{n/L_n}\,h_n^{s-2}\to0,
 \qquad q_{2,n}(\vartheta)\to0,
 \qquad q_{0,n}(\vartheta)/h_n\to0,
 \qquad
 \sqrt{n/L_n}\,q_{1,n}(\vartheta)q_{0,n}(\vartheta)\to0.
\tag{10}
\]
Conversely, if (10) holds for some fixed \(\vartheta>0\), (2) forces the lower inequality in (8), while the nonnegative term (4) forces
\(a_h<1/(6+4\vartheta)<1/6\).  At \(a_h=1/6\), (4) equals
\(a_h^{-1/2}\sqrt{\log n}\,n^{\vartheta/3}\) and diverges.  This proves that (8), with the upper endpoint excluded, is the maximal polynomial window when \(\vartheta\) is selected after \(a_h\).

The statement in the frozen core is the specialization \(\vartheta=1/4\).  In that case
\[
 q_{2,n}=q_{2,n}(1/4),\qquad
 q_{1,n}=q_{1,n}(1/4),\qquad
 q_{0,n}=q_{0,n}(1/4),
\]
and (5) becomes \(a_h<1/7\).  Equations (2)--(7) therefore prove exactly the three equivalences asserted there.  In this specialized window,
\[
 \frac{n h_n^7}{\log n}
 =\frac{n^{1-7a_h}}{\log n}\to\infty,
 \qquad
 \frac{n h_n^{13/2}}{\log n}
 =\frac{n^{1-(13/2)a_h}}{\log n}\to\infty,
\tag{11}
\]
because \(a_h<1/7<2/13\), and
\[
 n h_n^2L_n^2
 =a_h^2n^{1-2a_h}(\log n)^2\to\infty
\tag{12}
\]
because \(a_h<1/2\).  This proves every assertion of the target and, in addition, the directed maximal \(1/6\) parameterized window.

Fix \(P\in\mathcal F_s\).  Constants below depend only on the displayed class constants, the fixed kernel, \(J\), and the fixed grid separation, and hence are uniform in \(P\).  Under the maximal bandwidth post-image, choose a fixed \(\vartheta\) satisfying
\[
 0<\vartheta<\min\left\{1,\frac{a_h^{-1}-6}{4}\right\}.
\tag{1}
\]
Under the narrower frozen bandwidth assumption the same choice is available.  Define
\[
 U_{k,n}=q_{k,n}(\vartheta)
 =\left\{\frac{\log n}{n h_n^{2+2k+2\vartheta}}\right\}^{1/2}
  +h_n^{s-k-\vartheta},\qquad k=0,1,2.
\tag{2}
\]
Writing the stochastic and bias summands in (2) separately gives
\[
 \sqrt{\frac n{L_n}}
 \left\{\frac{\log n}{n h_n^{4+2\vartheta}}\right\}^{1/2}
 \left\{\frac{\log n}{n h_n^{2+2\vartheta}}\right\}^{1/2}
 =a_h^{-1/2}\sqrt{\log n}\,
   n^{-1/2+a_h(3+2\vartheta)},
\]
while either stochastic--bias cross term equals
\(a_h^{-1/2}h_n^{s-2-2\vartheta}\), and the bias--bias term equals
\(n^{1/2-a_h(2s-1-2\vartheta)}/\sqrt{a_h\log n}\).
By (1), the first exponent is negative; by \(s\geq8\), the remaining powers vanish.  The same direct calculation gives
\(q_{2,n}(\vartheta)=o(1)\) and
\(q_{0,n}(\vartheta)/h_n=o(1)\).  Therefore
\[
 U_{2,n}=o(1),\qquad U_{0,n}/h_n=o(1),
 \qquad \sqrt{n/L_n}\,U_{1,n}U_{0,n}=o(1).
\tag{3}
\]

We first prove the density-pilot estimates.  For a multi-index \(b\) of length \(|b|=m\), a centered summand of
\(D^b\widetilde f_g(x)-\mathbb E_PD^b\widetilde f_g(x)\) has envelope at most
\(C h_n^{-2-m}\) and variance at most \(C h_n^{-2-2m}\); these follow directly by the changes of variables
\(u=(x-z)/h_n\), using the compact support and smoothness of \(K\), and ass:density-positivity.  Bernstein's exponential-moment argument on a torus lattice of mesh \(h_n n^{-3}\), followed by the mean-value theorem between lattice points, therefore yields, for \(m=0,1,2,3\),
\[
 \mathbb E_P\left\|D^m\widetilde f_g-
       \mathbb E_PD^m\widetilde f_g\right\|_\infty^4
 \leq C\left\{\frac{\log n}{n h_n^{2+2m}}\right\}^{2}.
\tag{4}
\]
The Bernstein linear term is absorbed because
\(n h_n^2/\log n\to\infty\), which follows from \(a_h<1/6\).  The deterministic interpolation inequality
\[
 [D^k v]_{C^{0,\vartheta}}
 \leq C\|D^k v\|_\infty^{1-\vartheta}
          \|D^{k+1}v\|_\infty^{\vartheta}
\tag{5}
\]
and H\"older's inequality applied to (4) give
\[
 \mathbb E_P\left\|\widetilde f_g-\mathbb E_P\widetilde f_g
                   \right\|_{C^{k,\vartheta}}^4
 \leq C\left\{\frac{\log n}
 {n h_n^{2+2k+2\vartheta}}\right\}^{2},
 \qquad k=0,1,2.
\tag{6}
\]
Taylor's formula with integral remainder, ass:kernel-mass, and every vanishing moment in ass:kernel-order give
\[
 \left\|\mathbb E_P\widetilde f_g-f_g\right\|_{C^{k,\vartheta}}
 \leq C h_n^{s-k-\vartheta},
 \qquad k=0,1,2.
\tag{7}
\]
Combining (6)--(7), taking the maximum over the four cells, and using
\((x+y)^4\leq8(x^4+y^4)\), we obtain
\[
 \mathbb E_P\left[\max_g
 \|\widetilde f_g-f_g\|_{C^{k,\vartheta}}^4\right]
 \leq C U_{k,n}^4.
\tag{8}
\]
The same lattice argument at a fixed threshold, now applied directly to H\"older increments, gives
\[
 \mathbb P_P\left(\max_g
 \|\widetilde f_g-f_g\|_{C^{2,\vartheta}}>\epsilon_0\right)
 \leq C_0\exp\{-c_0n h_n^{6+2\vartheta}\}
\tag{9}
\]
after decreasing \(\epsilon_0\) and taking \(n\) large enough that the bias in (7) is below \(\epsilon_0/2\).  Polynomial lattice factors are absorbed because (1) implies
\(n h_n^{6+2\vartheta}/\log n\to\infty\).  Setting \(\vartheta=1/4\) in (8) with \(k=1\) and in the unabsorbed form of (9) gives exactly
\[
 \mathbb E_P\left[\max_g
 \|\widetilde f_g-f_g\|_{C^{1,1/4}}^4\right]
 \leq C\left\{\frac{\log n}{n h_n^{9/2}}
                  +h_n^{2s-5/2}\right\}^{2},
\tag{10}
\]
and
\[
 \mathbb P_P\left(\max_g
 \|\widetilde f_g-f_g\|_{C^{2,1/4}}>\epsilon_0\right)
 \leq C_0\exp\{-c_0n h_n^{13/2}\},
\tag{11}
\]
as asserted in the target.  Notice that the high-probability event used below is (9) with the post-bandwidth choice (1); formula (11) remains the requested valid fixed-H\"older bound.

We next establish the periodic Green decomposition.  Fix a grid point \(y\), write \(B_y=B(y)\), and choose a coordinate ball whose radius is less than one eighth of the grid-separation and cut-locus margins.  In that chart set
\[
 \Gamma_y(z)=-\frac1{2\pi\sqrt{\det B_y}}
       \log\left|B_y^{-1/2}(z-y)\right|.
\tag{12}
\]
Let \(\chi\) be supported in the chart and equal to one near \(y\), and define before testing
\[
 F_y(z)=\{B(z)-B_y\}\chi(z)\nabla\Gamma_y(z).
\tag{13}
\]
Uniform H\"older control of the population coefficients, obtained from the uniformly invertible augmented systems in thm:nested-derivative, gives
\[
 |F_y(z)|\leq C|z-y|^{-1+\vartheta},
 \qquad \|F_y\|_{L^2}\leq C,
\tag{14}
\]
where the second inequality follows from
\(\int_0^r t^{-2+2\vartheta}t\,dt<\infty\).  The coercive functional on
\(H_0^1\) with linear part \(v\mapsto-\int F_y\cdot\nabla v\), together with the bounded cutoff terms, has a unique minimizer \(w_y\); testing its weak Euler equation is now legitimate and gives
\(\|\nabla w_y\|_2\leq C\).  The difference between the normalized periodic Green function and
\(\chi\Gamma_y+w_y\) is \(B\)-harmonic on a smaller ball.  The interior estimate in lem:elliptic-green-gradient-bound bounds its gradient there, while compactness and the mean-zero energy estimate bound it outside the chart.  Applying the same estimate after rescaling dyadic annuli in (13) yields
\[
 \nabla_zG_B(y,z)=\nabla\Gamma_y(z)+R_y(z),
 \qquad |R_y(z)|\leq C|z-y|^{-1+\vartheta},
 \qquad \sup_y\|R_y\|_2\leq C.
\tag{15}
\]
This construction supplies the torus harmonic correction rather than treating the bounded-domain Green estimate as periodic.

Insert a centered cell-
\(g\) kernel tangent into def:nested-derivative and apply Fubini before taking norms.  The coefficient identity
\(BD^{-\mathsf T}=\alpha\mathsf C\) proved in thm:nested-derivative makes the order-one part, in the original cell coordinate, equal to
\[
 \psi^0_{g,j,h}(x)
 =K_h^{\mathrm{per}}*\zeta^0_{g,j}(x)
   -P_g(K_h^{\mathrm{per}}*\zeta^0_{g,j}),
\tag{16}
\]
where \(\zeta^0_{g,j}\) is the affine pullback of \(\nabla\Gamma_{y_j}\) with the appropriate smooth cell weight.  The exact change of variables in the transformed integral cancels the Jacobian in each transformed density tangent; thus (16) retains both appearances of every control-cell noise.

For any population pullback \(\Phi\), Taylor's formula gives, uniformly for \(|v|\leq Ch\),
\[
 \Phi(x+v)-\Phi(x)-D\Phi(x)v
 =\int_0^1(1-t)D^2\Phi(x+tv)[v,v],dt,
 \qquad |\Phi(x+v)-\Phi(x)-D\Phi(x)v|\leq Ch^2.
\tag{17}
\]
Equations (15)--(17), split over dyadic annuli about the transformed pole, show that replacing the variable coefficient and nonlinear coordinate by the field in (16) costs at most a uniform constant in \(L^2(P_g)\).  Explicitly, away from a ball of radius \(Ch\), kernel symmetry and (17) give
\[
 |K_h^{\mathrm{per}}*\zeta^0(x)-\zeta^0(x)|
 \leq Ch,d(x,x_0)^{-2},
\tag{18}
\]
whereas inside the ball the mollified field is at most \(C/h\).  Consequently
\[
 \int_{d\leq Ch}|K_h^{\mathrm{per}}*\zeta^0|^2=O(1),
 \qquad
 \int_{d>Ch}|K_h^{\mathrm{per}}*\zeta^0-\zeta^0|^2=O(1).
\tag{19}
\]
The order-minus-two nested term is bounded by the convolution of two first-order Green singularities:
\[
 C\int_{\mathbb T^2}
 \frac{dz}{d(z,y_j)d(z,x)}
 \leq C\{1+|\log d(x,y_j)|\},
\tag{20}
\]
which is uniformly square integrable.  The weighted-Hodge construction and bounded Riesz scores in thm:nested-derivative give the same uniform \(L^2\) bound for the full harmonic part.  Since
\(\|K_h^{\mathrm{per}}\|_1\leq\|K\|_1^2\), Young's inequality is now applied to already established \(L^2\) remainders, and (15)--(20) yield
\[
 \|\Psi_{g,h}-\psi^0_{g,h}\|_{L^2(P_g)}\leq C,
 \qquad
 \|\Psi_{g,h}\|_{L^2(P_g)}\leq C\sqrt{\log(1/h)}.
\tag{21}
\]
Moreover, the annular envelope is \(C/(d(x,x_0)+h)\).  Because
\[
 \int_0^1\frac{r}{(r+h)^4},dr\leq Ch^{-2},
\tag{22}
\]
finite \(J\), density boundedness, and (20) imply
\[
 \max_g\mathbb E_{P_g}\|\Psi_{g,h}(X)\|^4\leq Ch^{-2}.
\tag{23}
\]
Centering is harmless because \(d(\cdot,x_0)^{-1}\) is integrable in two dimensions.  Equations (21)--(23) prove the first score assertions, including the generated-target cross terms and nonzero harmonic modes.

We next control estimated coefficients and poles.  On the opposite-fold event (9), the stability of the two augmented scalar--harmonic systems in thm:nested-derivative, the mixed one-map estimate in lem:one-map-mixed-linearization, and (8) imply
\[
 \epsilon_n^{\mathrm{coef}}
 :=\max_{g,r}\left(
 \|\widehat B^{(-r)}-B\|_{C^1}
 +\|\widehat{\mathsf C}^{(-r)}-\mathsf C\|_{C^1}
 +\|\widehat\alpha^{(-r)}-\alpha\|_{C^1}
 \right)=o_{\mathbb P}(1),
\tag{24}
\]
and every transformed evaluation pole satisfies
\[
 d_n^{\mathrm{pole}}=O_{\mathbb P}(U_{0,n})=o_{\mathbb P}(h_n).
\tag{25}
\]
Here the first equality in (25) follows by applying the uniformly bounded augmented inverse to the density perturbation in \(C^{0,\vartheta}\), and the last equality is (3).  For a mollified \(1/d\) field, differentiation in the pole and the two-region calculation in (19) give
\[
 \|K_h^{\mathrm{per}}*\zeta^0(\,\cdot-d)
       -K_h^{\mathrm{per}}*\zeta^0\|_2
 \leq C|d|/h.
\tag{26}
\]
For the scalar inverses the resolvent identity is
\[
 \mathcal L_{\widehat B}^{-1}-\mathcal L_B^{-1}
 =\mathcal L_{\widehat B}^{-1}
   (\mathcal L_B-\mathcal L_{\widehat B})\mathcal L_B^{-1};
\tag{27}
\]
the finite-dimensional Schur complements obey the identical algebraic identity.  Uniform coercivity from thm:nested-derivative, (21), and (24) show that coefficient changes cost at most
\(C\epsilon_n^{\mathrm{coef}}\sqrt{L_n}\) in score norm.  Equations (25)--(27), together with the bounded order-minus-two and harmonic envelopes, therefore give conditionally on the training fold and hence unconditionally
\[
 \max_{g,r}\,L_n^{-1/2}
 \|\widehat\Psi_{g,h_n}^{(-r)}-\Psi_{g,h_n}\|_{L^2(P_g)}
 =o_{\mathbb P}(1).
\tag{28}
\]
The first maximum in (28) is over \(g\in\mathcal G\) and the second over
\(r\in\{1,2\}\).  The estimated analog of the annular envelope in (22) holds on (9) with the same constant, so
\[
 \max_{g,r}\mathbb E_{P_g}
 \|\widehat\Psi_{g,h_n}^{(-r)}(X)\|^4\leq Ch_n^{-2}
\tag{29}
\]
on events with probability tending to one uniformly.

It remains to establish the nonlinear remainder with the correct two endpoints.  For a zero-integral perturbation \(u=(u_g)_g\), set
\[
 U_k(u)=\max_g\|u_g\|_{C^{k,\vartheta}},\qquad k=0,1,2.
\tag{30}
\]
Assume the perturbed densities are positive and \(U_2(u)<\epsilon_0\).  In the augmented equations from thm:nested-derivative, subtract the equation at \(P\) and its first derivative.  Reciprocal terms have the exact remainder
\[
 \frac1{f+u}-\frac1f+\frac{u}{f^2}
 =\frac{u^2}{f^2(f+u)},
\tag{31}
\]
bounded by \(C U_1(u)U_0(u)\) using positivity and
\(U_0(u)\leq U_1(u)\).  Product remainders contain one differentiated perturbation and one undifferentiated perturbation and have the same bound.  For compositions, the integral identity
\[
 v(x+d)-v(x)=\int_0^1Dv(x+td)d\,dt
\tag{32}
\]
shows that the post-linearization remainder is bounded by
\(C U_1(u)\|d\|_\infty+C\|d\|_\infty^2\); the augmented inverse gives
\(\|d\|_\infty\leq C U_0(u)\).  The determinant and scalar-potential terms are precisely the two-endpoint remainder controlled by lem:one-map-mixed-linearization, hence are also at most \(C U_1(u)U_0(u)\).  Finally, differentiating the weighted-Hodge reduced-cost stationarity equations shows that every harmonic residual is a bilinear integral with one coefficient or gradient perturbation and one displacement perturbation; uniform coercivity and Cauchy--Schwarz again bound it by \(C U_1(u)U_0(u)\).  Applying the uniformly bounded augmented inverse from thm:nested-derivative first to the inner system, propagating that solution through the exact generated density, and then applying it to the outer system gives
\[
 \max_{1\leq j\leq J}
 \left\|
 \widetilde T_{P+u}(\widetilde y_j)-\widetilde T_P(\widetilde y_j)
 -\mathcal D_P[u]_j
 \right\|
 \leq C U_1(u)U_0(u).
\tag{33}
\]
This is the required mixed \(C^{1,\vartheta}\)-times-
\(C^{0,\vartheta}\) estimate, including both harmonic translations.  It implies the frozen target's displayed squared \(C^{1,1/4}\) bound by taking \(\vartheta=1/4\) and using
\(U_0(u)\leq U_1(u)\).

For the KDE perturbation, (8), Cauchy--Schwarz, and (33) give the explicit probability and risk controls
\[
 \sqrt{n/L_n}\,U_{1,n}U_{0,n}=o(1),
 \qquad
 \mathbb E_P\|\operatorname{Rem}_n\|^2
 \leq C U_{1,n}^2U_{0,n}^2.
\tag{34}
\]
The deterministic order-\(s\) kernel bias is sent by the order-minus-two derivative to
\(O(h_n^{s-2})\), and (2) of the bandwidth proof makes
\(\sqrt{n/L_n}h_n^{s-2}\to0\).

Finally, on (9), decrease \(\epsilon_0\) below \(c/2\).  Then clipping is inactive.  Periodization and ass:kernel-mass give
\(\int_{\mathbb T^2}\widetilde f_g=1\), so the normalizer is exactly one.  Uniform augmented-system stability, ass:lift-regularity, and (24)--(25) keep both estimated maps on the selected population branches, preserve uniform ellipticity, and put every pilot pole at distance
\(o_{\mathbb P}(h_n)\) from its population pole.  Equations (8)--(11), (21)--(29), and (33)--(34) prove all assertions of the target, with the directed mixed remainder replacing the obsolete squared-rate calculation.

proposed.name: \(a_h\)
proposed.def: The fixed polynomial bandwidth exponent in the maximal mixed-remainder window.

proposed_core_edits.reason: The mixed stochastic--stochastic remainder is negligible for a fixed positive Hölder exponent chosen after \(a_h\) exactly when \(a_h<1/6\); the endpoint is excluded.

novel.justification: This synchronized window balances the order-minus-two bias and the mixed two-endpoint nonlinear remainder. For each bandwidth exponent below the open upper endpoint, a fixed positive Hölder index can be selected so that pilot consistency, moving-pole stability, and the normalized mixed remainder hold; at the upper endpoint the stochastic--stochastic product diverges for every positive Hölder index.

proposed_core_edits.reason: The proved parameterized Hölder calculation gives the maximal open upper endpoint \(1/6\), while retaining the bias lower endpoint \(1/[2(s-2)]\).
